source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client is confused from long bed rest and may now walk as tolerated. What is BEST?
questions.rationale: The confusion comes from bed rest and low stimulation; walking in the hall increases sensory input.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q881 (PDF p. 1121)
questions.quote: The cause of the client’s confusion is bed rest and decreased sensory stimulation from a prolonged length of stay

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with paralytic ileus is upset about needing an NG tube. Which response shows empathy?
questions.rationale: Empathy shares the client's frame of reference and helps express feelings.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q903 (PDF p. 1146)
questions.quote: In option 3, the nurse uses empathy.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A new diabetic is anxious about self-injecting insulin. What is a good FIRST step?
questions.rationale: The nurse may select the site and insert the needle, with the client pushing the plunger as a first step to self-injection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q967 (PDF p. 1215)
questions.quote: Some clients find it difficult to insert a needle into their own skin.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When should crutch walking be taught for knee surgery?
questions.rationale: Crutch walking is taught before surgery because learning is hard when in pain and not fully alert.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1074 (PDF p. 1356)
questions.quote: It is best to assess crutch-walking ability and instruct the client with regard to the use of the crutches before surgery

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the focus when assessing an older client's functional status?
questions.rationale: Functional status is the ability to perform ADLs: bathing, toileting, ambulating, dressing, and feeding.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1112 (PDF p. 1396)
questions.quote: the nurse assesses the client’s ability to perform self-care or ADLs

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY problem for a client in Buck's traction?
questions.rationale: Immobility poses the greatest risk of complications. Buck's is skin traction, so infection risk is low.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1124 (PDF p. 1408)
questions.quote: The priority client problem in Buck’s traction is immobility.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How is infection risk reduced for TPN via a central line?
options: Use the line for blood draws
questions.rationale: CVCs are a direct entry to the heart and circulation, so sterile technique is vital for dressing changes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1143 (PDF p. 1429)
questions.quote: Sterile technique is vital during dressing changes of a central venous catheter (CVC).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How does a client in a lower-extremity spica cast use the bedpan?
questions.rationale: The client cannot bend at the hips, so a low-profile fracture pan is used.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1144 (PDF p. 1431)
questions.quote: A low-profile bedpan or fracture pan is designed for use by clients with body or leg casts

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which intervention limits complications of prolonged bed rest?
questions.rationale: Immobility promotes calcium stones; limiting milk products helps prevent them. Supine positioning raises risks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1149 (PDF p. 1436)
questions.quote: Limiting milk and milk products is the best measure to prevent the formation of calcium stones.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A stroke client has ROM ordered for the right side. What should the home nurse plan?
questions.rationale: All forms of ROM are considered; the client can assist in his own care, promoting independence.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1175 (PDF p. 1464)
questions.quote: the client can assist with some of his or her own rehabilitative care.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY before giving an NG tube feeding?
questions.rationale: NG tubes can migrate; placement is verified before anything is instilled.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1182 (PDF p. 1472)
questions.quote: The nurse avoids injecting any substance into a client’s NGT before verifying tube placement

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Give 7.5 mg IM; the label reads 10 mg/mL. How many mL?
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1184 (PDF p. 1475)
questions.quote: After performing a medication calculation problem, ensure that the answer or the amount of medication to be admin

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After hip fixation, a client's left heel is red. Which equipment helps?
questions.rationale: The redness comes from pressure against the mattress; an alternating pressure mattress minimizes pressure points.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1186 (PDF p. 1477)
questions.quote: An alternating pressure mattress is effective at minimizing pressure points.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which suction pressure is used for an infant's tracheostomy?
questions.rationale: Infants and children need smaller catheters and lower suction settings than adults; about 90 mm Hg for an infant.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1196 (PDF p. 1488)
questions.quote: Suctioning in infants and children requires the use of a smaller suction catheter and lower suction settings

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client starts seizing in bed. How is aspiration prevented?
options: Turn on side, head flexed forward
questions.rationale: Side-lying with the head flexed lets the tongue fall forward and secretions drain.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1197 (PDF p. 1489)
questions.quote: Positioning the client on one side with the head flexed forward allows the tongue to fall forward

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which item is essential for moving a client in leg traction?
questions.rationale: A trapeze lets the client lift straight up without altering the traction pull.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1203 (PDF p. 1495)
questions.quote: A trapeze is essential to allow the client to lift straight up while being moved

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which lab result is MOST important to report for a client on TPN?
questions.rationale: The provider uses electrolyte values to formulate the TPN solution.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1207 (PDF p. 1499)
questions.quote: Total parenteral nutrition solutions contain amino acids and dextrose in solution with electrolytes

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is the BEST indicator of nutritional status during enteral feeding?
questions.rationale: Prealbumin is the most important parameter for nutritional effectiveness; it reflects recent changes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1235 (PDF p. 1528)
questions.quote: A serum prealbumin level is the most important parameter for determining the effectiveness

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding MOST reliably shows a post-op NG tube to suction is working?
questions.rationale: The tube decompresses the bowel; flowing drainage with no abdominal distention shows function.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1237 (PDF p. 1530)
questions.quote: An NG tube connected to suction is used postoperatively to decompress and rest the bowel.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An antibiotic vial makes 2 g in 5 mL after mixing. How many mL for 650 mg?
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1254 (PDF p. 1554)
questions.quote: Convert 2 g to mg and then use the formula for calculating medication doses.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How is an oropharyngeal airway inserted in an adult?
questions.rationale: The airway is inserted tip up and rotated down once the flange reaches the teeth, with the neck hyperextended.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1287 (PDF p. 1587)
questions.quote: The airway is inserted with the tip pointed upward and is then rotated downward

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which statement after a stress management seminar needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Confrontation is a communication technique and may increase stress; the others are stress management techniques.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1293 (PDF p. 1594)
questions.quote: Confrontation is a communication technique, not a stress management technique.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding shows the lung has fully re-expanded with a chest tube?
questions.rationale: With full expansion, no air remains to cause fluctuation (tidaling) in the water-seal chamber.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1301 (PDF p. 1602)
questions.quote: When the lung has completely expanded, there is no longer air in the pleural space

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which method effectively prevents STIs?
questions.rationale: Effective measures are abstinence, correct condom use, and avoiding multiple partners.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1335 (PDF p. 1637)
questions.quote: Effective measures to avoid STIs include abstinence, using condoms properly, and avoiding multiple partners

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which exercise BEST strengthens the lower back?
questions.rationale: Walking and swimming strengthen back muscles; twisting and pulling activities do not help.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1337 (PDF p. 1640)
questions.quote: Walking and swimming are very beneficial in strengthening back muscles

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How does a woman prepare for a midstream urine culture?
questions.rationale: The perineum is cleansed front to back with antiseptic swabs; the midstream portion is collected in a sterile cup.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1397 (PDF p. 1701)
questions.quote: the client cleanses the perineum from front to back using antiseptic swabs.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement shows parents understand home colostomy care for Hirschsprung's disease?
questions.rationale: Parents report skin breakdown or stomal problems, such as ribbonlike stools or failure to pass flatus or stool.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1407 (PDF p. 1713)
questions.quote: stomal complications, such as ribbonlike stools or failure to pass flatus or stools

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is routine chest tube care?
options: Keep the unit above the chest
questions.rationale: Coughing and deep breathing aid lung expansion; water is added to the suction chamber as needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1426 (PDF p. 1735)
questions.quote: The client is encouraged to cough and deep breathe to assist in lung expansion.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which items are gathered for tracheostomy care?
questions.rationale: Equipment includes a trach care kit, sterile water and saline, and a suction kit.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1434 (PDF p. 1743)
questions.quote: Equipment needed to perform tracheostomy care includes a tracheostomy care kit, sterile water and saline solutions

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the safe wall suction range for an adult tracheostomy?
questions.rationale: The safe adult range is 80 to 120 mm Hg, with hyperoxygenation before and after.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1447 (PDF p. 1756)
questions.quote: The safe wall suction range for an adult is 80 to 120 mm Hg

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is an iron injection given?
questions.rationale: Parenteral iron is given deep in the gluteal muscle by Z-track to prevent staining and irritation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1453 (PDF p. 1762)
questions.quote: The correct technique for administering parenteral iron is deep in the gluteal muscle using Z-track technique

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on inhaled albuterol cannot cough up secretions. What helps MOST?
questions.rationale: Increased fluids (2000–3000 mL/day unless contraindicated) thin secretions.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1471 (PDF p. 1780)
questions.quote: The client should take in increased fluids (2000 to 3000 mL/day unless contraindicated)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which crutch statement needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Only crutches measured for the client are used unless adjusted to fit.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1486 (PDF p. 1795)
questions.quote: Crutches belonging to another person should not be used unless they have been adjusted to fit the client.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is a new trach tube holder checked for proper tightness?
questions.rationale: Two fingers should slide comfortably under the holder: secure but not too tight.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1506 (PDF p. 1815)
questions.quote: There should be enough room for two fingers to slide comfortably under the tracheostomy holder.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Ibuprofen 0.4 g is ordered; tablets are 200 mg. How many tablets?
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1530 (PDF p. 1840)
questions.quote: Convert 0.4 g to mg.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What should the nurse do before giving a Mantoux test?
questions.rationale: The nurse explains the test and asks about prior positive reactions; it is not given if there was one. It is given intradermally with a tuberculin syringe.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1550 (PDF p. 1863)
questions.quote: The test should not be administered if the client has such a history.
